summary: Iteration 4 — Multi-profile Household refactor verified. 20/20 executed backend tests passed (1 intentionally skipped to avoid destructive last-profile deletion of seeded data). Strict per-profile data isolation confirmed via X-Profile-Id: items/outfits/plans/wear/laundry created under 'Aura' (prof_365ddfe52deb) are invisible to 'David' (prof_a82ae0522746) and vice-versa; cross-profile GET/{id} → 404, cross-profile PUT/{id} → 404, cross-profile DELETE is a silent no-op (owned resource remains). Omitting X-Profile-Id resolves to the earliest-created profile (Aura) — verified item lists match exactly. Profile CRUD works end-to-end: POST /api/profiles (creates prof_ id, echoes name/emoji), PUT /api/profiles/{id} (rename+emoji change), DELETE /api/profiles/{id} (also purges the profile's items/outfits/plans/wear_logs). PUT /api/profile scoped to the active profile only — updating David's body_shape/notes did NOT touch Aura's style block. NEW: POST /api/analyze-item accepts optional category_hint and correctly forces category='Tops' when hint='Tops'; still works without the hint (backward compatible, 200 both ways). Regression on scoped AI + data endpoints under X-Profile-Id: stylist/suggest (Aura=200 with resolved_items; David empty wardrobe=200), items/{id}/compatibility, capsule/build, packing/plan (offsets 0 and 14), insights/missing-piece, insights/health-report, GET /insights, GET /laundry — all 200. Laundry per-profile: item flipped to Washing appears in Aura's /laundry only, not David's; reset to Ready removes it. Wear + plans CRUD also isolated. Post-run cleanup verified clean state: 0 TEST_ items, 0 laundry items, 0 leftover profiles beyond the 2 seeded ones.

minor.issue: Cross-profile DELETE is a silent no-op (returns {ok:true} without indicating nothing was matched). Owned resource is not affected, so this is safe, but a 404 would be more explicit. Carried over from iter 2/3.
Return 200 on creation instead of 201 (convention). Carried over from iter 2/3.

ProfileUpdate skips None entries — sending {measurements: null} does NOT clear the field. Cannot fully reset a profile's style back to {} without direct DB access; empty strings ('') can be persisted but 'null' cannot. Documented in iter-3 code review; still applies.

action_items: None required — multi-profile refactor and analyze-item category_hint feature verified working end-to-end.

Optional cleanup: David profile now has body_shape='' and notes='' as harmless residue from the isolation test (cannot be cleared to null via PUT /api/profile due to None-skipping in ProfileUpdate). If a fully-empty profile.profile is desired, reset via direct DB update or extend PUT to accept explicit clears.
Optional (carried over): return 201 from creation endpoints; return 404 from delete-on-missing; wrap LLM chat.send_message with asyncio.wait_for; split server.py (1184 lines) into routers.
critical_code_review_comments: get_scope (server.py:115-133) correctly returns user_id = profile_id, so all existing data queries scope per-profile with no per-endpoint refactor needed — clean design.

ensure_default_profile (server.py:89-112) auto-creates a default profile on first access AND migrates legacy documents (user_id==account_id) to the new profile id. This is a one-shot migration; safe for existing accounts, and it correctly runs when GET /api/profiles is called with no rows.
DELETE /api/profiles/{id} (server.py:258-267) cascades and removes items/outfits/wear_logs/plans owned by that profile — matches spec.
Last-profile guard (server.py:260-262) raises 400 if count<=1. Correct behaviour by inspection; not asserted destructively in tests (would delete seeded profiles).
PUT /api/profiles/{id} (rename) uses `payload.dict()` filter for None — so passing empty string DOES update. Consistent with PUT /api/profile.

analyze-item category_hint prompt (server.py:445-450) is passed as user text; category_hint is NOT sanitized against the enum server-side. If FE sends an invalid category, the LLM will simply reflect it. Consider validating hint against the Tops/Bottoms/... allowed set.
